etymologies.etymologyHTML: accuracy (countable and uncountable, plural accuracies)

definitions.definition: The state of being accurate; being free from error; exactness; correctness

quote.citation: 1827, Thomas Reid, Essays on the Powers of the Human Mind:
quote.text: Its professed end [of logic], is to teach men to think, to judge, and to reason, with precision and accuracy.

quote.citation: 1856, Dionysius Lardner, Popular Lectures on Science and Art:
quote.text: The efficiency of the instrument will also depend upon the accuracy with which the piston fits the bottom and sides of the barrel. When the piston is depressed to the bottom, it is considered in theory to be in absolute contact, so as to exclude every particle of air from the space between it and the bottom.

quote.citation: 1907 August, Robert W[illiam] Chambers, chapter VIII, in The Younger Set, New York, N.Y.: D. Appleton & Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: At her invitation he outlined for her the succeeding chapters with terse military accuracy ; and what she liked best and best understood was avoidance of that false modesty which condescends, turning technicality into pabulum.

definitions.definition: Exact conformity to truth, or to a rule or model; degree of conformity of a measure to a true or standard value.
